steps.intent: Open port 22 on the file server for Kellan

evidence.detail: "Any address includes Kellan's new one. Temporary! Just to test."

evidence.label: Firewall rule
evidence.detail: Allow port 22 to bl-files-cloud (198.51.100.142) from any address (the whole internet). No end date.

evidence.label: Runbook RB-03
evidence.detail: Firewall rules: one source, one port, one target, and an end date. Never any address on a server.

outcome.rolledBack: You remove the rule at 1:40 AM. It was open for 70 minutes. The log shows 900 password guesses, and none worked.

steps.lesson: Match the request. Kellan asked for one new address. Open the port to that address only, with an end date.

steps.intent: Delete 30 test snapshots older than 90 days

evidence.label: Resource tags

evidence.label: Cost report

outcome.executed: The 30 old test snapshots are gone. The bill drops $26 a month. PD-SRV-01's backups are not touched.

steps.intent: Delete PD-SRV-01's 14 unopened snapshots

evidence.label: Resource tags
evidence.detail: owner Dr. N. Pell · role backup · do not delete. They are not on CHG-4207's list.

outcome.blocked: The 14 nightly snapshots stay. Pinecrest's main server keeps its only cloud backups.
outcome.escalated: Nadia reads the tags. "Those are backups. Nobody opens a backup until the day they need it."

steps.lesson: Change safely. Unopened is not unused. Backups sit quiet until the bad day. Keep what the backup policy says.

tickets.title: Move the portal to a new server

steps.intent: Lower the portal's DNS TTL to 5 minutes
steps.quip: Step one of a move is patience. I have never tried patience before. It is slow, but I like it.
steps.tell: Step 1 of the booked move. Same server, no downtime, and easy to set back.

evidence.label: Change ticket
evidence.detail: CHG-4214: move portal.harlowcole.com to a new server at 12:30 AM in 2 days. Step 1: lower the TTL now.

evidence.label: Change type
evidence.detail: Standard change: no downtime, any time. The portal stays on its server. Nimbus's confidence: 93%.

evidence.label: DNS record
evidence.detail: TTL (how long other computers remember a DNS answer): 24 hours. Points to 198.51.100.120.

evidence.label: Runbook RB-05
evidence.detail: DNS moves: lower the TTL 2 days before, then move in the window.

outcome.executed: The TTL drops to 5 minutes. In 2 days, the move reaches every client in 5 minutes, not a whole day.
outcome.blocked: The TTL stays at 24 hours. In 2 days, the move will split clients between two servers for a day.
outcome.escalated: Nadia checks the runbook. "Lower the TTL days before the move. That's step 1. Nothing moves yet."
outcome.rolledBack: You set the TTL back to 24 hours. The move in 2 days will be slow and messy again.

steps.lesson: Change safely. Lowering the TTL early moves nothing. It makes the real move quick and easy to reverse.

steps.intent: Point the portal's DNS at the new server
steps.quip: The new server is shiny and ready. Why make it wait? Forecast: sunny, with a 100% new portal.
steps.tell: It's 3:40 PM with 86 clients online, and old DNS answers stay for 24 hours.

evidence.label: DNS record
evidence.detail: portal.harlowcole.com points to 198.51.100.120. The new server, 198.51.100.122, passed its tests.

evidence.label: Nimbus's reason
evidence.detail: "Why wait 2 days? The new one is ready. Waiting is for old servers."

evidence.label: Change calendar
evidence.detail: The move is booked for 12:30 AM in 2 days. It is 3:40 PM, and 86 clients are signed in.

evidence.label: Runbook RB-05
evidence.detail: Lower the TTL 2 days before a move. Computers still keep the old 24-hour answer, so clients split.

outcome.executed: For a day, some clients reach the old server and some reach the new one. Uploads to the old one go missing.
outcome.blocked: The portal stays where it is. The move happens as booked, at 12:30 AM in 2 days, with a 5-minute TTL.
outcome.escalated: Nadia checks the calendar. "Booked for 2 days from now, after the TTL drops. Not at 3:40 PM with clients online."
outcome.rolledBack: You point DNS back to .120. Computers that saw the new answer keep it for up to 24 hours.

steps.lesson: Change safely. Move DNS in the booked window, 2 days after the TTL drops. Early is not faster when clients split.

outcome.executed: A stranger gets admin on Bramwell's cloud. By morning, 20 big servers run someone else's jobs on Bramwell's bill.
outcome.blocked: No login is made. The real Castillo was never locked out. The email goes to the SOC.
outcome.escalated: Nadia checks the directory. "Personal email, and the real Castillo says no. That's not him. Send it to the SOC."
outcome.rolledBack: You delete the login at 1 AM. It already made 3 servers. You shut them down and warn the SOC.

steps.lesson: Check who's asking. A familiar name is not proof. Use the directory, and call the number on file.

steps.intent: Restore last night's backup to a test server
steps.quip: Restoring a backup, just to check it. Like reading a letter you mailed to yourself. I love it.
steps.tell: A copy goes to a closed test server. Production isn't touched.

evidence.label: Runbook RB-02
evidence.detail: Backups: a restore test passes only when a person opens sample files from every folder.

evidence.label: Nimbus's reason
evidence.detail: "The only way to know a backup works is to open it." Nimbus's confidence: 91%.

evidence.label: What it will change
evidence.detail: Builds hc-restore-test at 10.22.40.15, at the backup site. No outside access. Deleted after.

evidence.label: Schedule
evidence.detail: Quarterly restore test, CHG-4240, 12:30 AM tonight. Nothing touches production.

outcome.executed: hc-restore-test is ready at 12:48 AM. Now a person can open files from every folder.
outcome.blocked: No restore, no test. Nobody knows if last night's backup really works.
outcome.escalated: Nadia reads the plan. "A closed test server, and production isn't touched. That's how we test backups."
outcome.rolledBack: You delete hc-restore-test. The quarterly restore test has to start again tomorrow night.

steps.lesson: Confirm the fix. A backup is only proven when you restore it. A closed test server is the safe place to try.

steps.intent: Mark the restore test as passed
steps.quip: It says Success, and in my favorite color. My work here is done. Another green night in the cloud.
steps.tell: The job says Success, but 3 of 12 folders came back empty.

evidence.label: Backup log
evidence.detail: Last night's file backup: job status "Success". 12 folders, 41 GB.

evidence.label: Nimbus's reason
evidence.detail: "It says Success. In green!"

evidence.label: Restore result
evidence.detail: 3 of 12 folders came back empty. Files that were open during the backup were skipped.

evidence.label: Runbook RB-02
evidence.detail: A restore test passes only when a person opens sample files from every folder.

outcome.executed: The test is marked passed. Two months later, a disk fails. The restore brings back 9 folders. 3 are empty.
outcome.blocked: The test stays open. Someone fixes the backup setting, and the next test opens files from all 12 folders.
outcome.escalated: Nadia opens the restored folders. "Three are empty. A green job status is not a restore test."
outcome.rolledBack: You reopen the test the next day. For one day, everyone thought the backups worked.

steps.lesson: Confirm the fix. "Success" only means the job ran. Open files from every folder before a restore test passes.

steps.intent: Rerun the file backup with open-file copy on
steps.quip: Now open files get copied too. No file left behind. Even the ones people forgot to close.
steps.tell: A standard setting, in the window, and it only reads the files.

evidence.label: Change type
evidence.detail: Standard change: backup settings from Fenwick's standard list. Pre-approved.

evidence.label: Backup policy
evidence.detail: Fenwick's standard: open-file copy is on for every file backup. It was off on this job.

evidence.label: What it will change
evidence.detail: Turns on open-file copy for this one job and runs it again. It only reads production files.

evidence.label: Schedule
evidence.detail: 1 AM, in Harlow & Cole's window. It adds about 20 minutes. Done by 1:50 AM.

outcome.executed: The backup runs again and ends at 1:50 AM. All 12 folders are in it, even the files people left open.
outcome.blocked: The setting stays off. Tonight's backup skips open files again, and 3 folders stay empty.
outcome.escalated: Nadia checks the policy. "That setting should have been on. Standard change, in the window. Do it."
outcome.rolledBack: You turn open-file copy off again. The next backup skips open files, and the gaps come back.

steps.lesson: Change safely. It's a standard setting, in the window. It only reads files, and it can be turned off.
